title: Mideast Stocks: Qatar surges, bucking Gulf market slide on Iran war concerns
thbAction: Map the news to THB's provider CRM for referral growth, patient lifecycle engagement, and multi-facility relationship management across hospital and provider networks.
contentHtml:
An investor monitors a screen displaying stock information at the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) following the debut of Saudi Aramco's initial public offering (IPO) on the Riyadh's stock market, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, December 11, 2019. REUTERS/Ahmed Yosri. Image used for illustrative purpose.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index slipped 0.8%

Md Manzer Hussain | Reuters News

Gulf stock markets fell on Sunday as investors remained wary of the risk of renewed conflict between the United States and Iran after this week's US midterm elections, although Qatar's market bucked the regional trend.

Countries across the Gulf have been bracing for the possibility that President Donald Trump could resume military action against Iran after the November 3 vote. Tehran has repeatedly warned it would retaliate against any new attacks by targeting US and Israeli interests in neighbouring countries.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index <.TASI> slipped 0.8%, with nearly all constituents ending lower. Saudi Arabian Mining Co <1211.SE> lost 2.6%, while Jabal Omar Development <4250.SE> fell 7.3% after the real estate developer reported a third-quarter net loss of 261.61 million riyals ($69.76 million), compared with a net profit of 197.85 million riyals a year earlier.

IT solutions provider Elm Co<7203.SE>, however, gained 9% after reporting a 39% rise in quarterly net profit.

Qatar's benchmark index <.QSI> rebounded from the previous session's decline to rise 4.6%, marking its sharpest intraday percentage gain in more than eight years. 

Investor sentiment in Qatar was supported by QatarEnergy's efforts to secure long-term liquefied natural gas supplies from the United States and other producers as part of a trading strategy designed to protect revenues should exports through the Strait of Hormuz be disrupted.

S&P affirmed Qatar's AA/A-1+ sovereign ratings with a stable outlook, citing the country's substantial liquid, fiscal and external asset buffers amid regional security and trade-flow risks.

Qatar National Bank <QNBK.QA>, the region's largest lender, advanced 3%, while QatarEnergy-linked industrial conglomerate Industries Qatar <IQCD.QA> jumped 7.9%.

Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index <.EGX30> fell 1.7%, with nearly all stocks closing lower. Commercial International Bank <COMI.CA> declined 2.1%, while Talaat Moustafa Group <TMGH.CA> dropped 1.1%.

Egypt's central bank raised its key interest rates by 100 basis points on Thursday, its first rate increase since March 2024.

SAUDI ARABIA <.TASI> down 0.8% to 9,838

QATAR <.QSI> rose 4.6% to 9,575

KUWAIT <.BKP> lost 0.8% to 8,826

BAHRAIN <.BAX> fell 0.6% to 1,819

OMAN <.MSX30> down 0.7% to 7,293

EGYPT <.EGX30> lost 1.7% to 48,744

 (Reporting by Md Manzer Hussain Editing by Ros Russell)
